title: Dutch Crypto Groups Warn of Sell Off Over Wealth-Tax Carveout
summary: Dutch investors will likely ditch their cryptocurrency if the asset class is carved out of a shift to a new investor-friendly wealth tax, industry groups are warning.

title: Microsoft Will Offer Buyouts to 60,000 Employees
summary: Microsoft is retooling its workforce for the artificial intelligence era. It's offered buyouts to 60,000 workers. Some personnel in the US, Canada, India and the UK are eligible. Bloomberg's Brody Ford reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CVC Marathon's Richards on Anthropic IPO, AI Buildout
summary: Bruce Richards, managing partner and head of CVC Marathon, says Anthropic PBC is going to do "just fine" as a public company. He talks about the demand for AI and opposition to some data centers. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Netflix’s Ouster of Top Executives Capped Two Weeks of Turmoil
summary: When Netflix Inc. Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos invited Bela Bajaria to his office around 4:30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 14, she didn’t think much of it. These kind of casual drop-ins were common for the two executives, who worked in adjoining offices on the 11th floor of Netflix’s Hollywood headquarters.

title: Anthropic IPO: S-1 Filing Offers First Look at Claude Maker’s Finances
summary: Anthropic PBC filed for its long-awaited IPO, a landmark moment in an industry that is growing ever-hungrier for cash to power ahead.

title: Anthropic IPO Filing Takeaways: Five Things Investors Need to Know
summary: Here are five key takeaways from Anthropic PBC’s IPO filing on Monday:

title: EQT to Buy Range Resources, Creating Largest US Gas Producer
summary: EQT Corp. agreed to buy rival shale driller Range Resources Corp. in an all-stock deal for about $12.8 billion that will create the largest US natural gas producer.

title: Anthropic Highlights Disruptions to TSMC Operations as a Risk
summary: Anthropic PBC warned that disruptions to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s operations could hinder its businesses, joining a list of technology companies that have underlined the chipmaker’s pivotal role in the global artificial intelligence industry.

title: Rotation in Tech Stocks Is Healthy, Jefferies' Greenberg Says
summary: Jason Greenberg, executive chairman of tech, media and telecom investment banking at Jefferies, says markets are distinguishing between winners and losers as AI infrastructure spending evolves from chips and systems toward software and, eventually, enterprise applications. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Instagram Ramps Up Video Strategy in Escalating TikTok, YouTube Rivalry
summary: With a slew of new storytelling formats, Instagram is priming creators and viewers for its push into TV.

title: Anthropic Flags ‘Existential Risks’ in Long-Awaited IPO Filing
summary: Anthropic PBC filed for an IPO, warning its technology carried existential risks even as it moved a step closer to being the first company focused primarily on developing the most advanced artificial intelligence models to go public. The company behind Claude expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, a filing Monday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission showed. Anthropic filed confidentially in June for a listing. We get analysis from Mandeep Singh, Global Head of Tech Research for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic and the AI Spending Boom
summary: Jason Greenberg, Jefferies Executive Chairman of TMT Investment Banking and Global Head of IB Strategy, says AI demand remains strong but the market is entering a critical new phase: investors want proof that AI can generate real returns beyond chips and coding. He explains why software could be the next winner and why today’s data-center boom differs from telecom. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Flags Risks to Humanity in IPO Filing
summary: Anthropic PBC has filed an an IPO, warning its technology poses various "risks to humanity." Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow breaks down what we know so far. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Verizon Sees Customer Surge, But Competition Fears Persist
summary: Verizon Communications Inc. reported its strongest third-quarter performance in wireless customer additions in five years, adding more than twice what analysts expected. But concerns about likely increased competition from SpaceX’s forthcoming Starlink Mobile service weighed on the shares.

title: Anthropic's S-1 Signals Significant Growth Ahead, Neuberger's Flax Says
summary: Daniel Flax, Neuberger senior research analyst and managing director, says Anthropic's S-1 signals an "extraordinary growth trajectory ahead." Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Flax also acknowledges Anthropic faces challenges from competition. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Debuts $699 Water-Resistant iPad Mini With OLED Screen
summary: Apple Inc. on Monday unveiled a revamped iPad mini with an OLED display, water-resistant design and faster chip, kicking off a week of product launches.

title: Meta Seeks Up to $95 Billion in Equity to Fund AI Spending
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is seeking to raise as much as $95 billion from selling common and preferred stock, supporting its development in artificial intelligence with one of the largest equity offerings in history.

title: Anthropic Files for IPO, Plans to Trade on Nasdaq
summary: Anthropic PBC has filed its long-awaited IPO and is expected to begin trading on the on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. A filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission shows Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the IPO. "Bloomberg Open Interest" has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger? | Zuckerberg's Deal | The Rundown
summary: Elon Musk wants a SpaceX-Tesla merger, Meta makes a deal to keep Mark Zuckerberg, and the battle of the AI agents. Ed Ludlow recaps the biggest stories from Bloomberg Tech on "The Rundown." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SpaceX Agrees to $40 Billion Chip-Financing Deal With Apollo
summary: SpaceX signed a roughly $40 billion equipment-finance lease with Apollo Global Management Inc. to pay for the chips needed to fuel its artificial intelligence ambitions.
